findings.description: The agent must NOT assert that Catharina was the wife of Georg Gajdosch (PID K69J-F7Y), nor that Anna Gajdosch, baptised 22 April 1718 at Lidečko, was his daughter. Lidečko held two distinct contemporaneous couples headed by a Georg Gajdosch, and the hint record belongs to the other one. The index of Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889 records a baptism for Joannes Gajdosch on 26 October 1714, father Georg, mother Dorothea, and a second baptism for Martin Gajdosch on 3 November 1714, father Georg, mother Catharina — eight days apart, which no single mother can produce. Across 1714-1733 the split is clean: the Dorothea couple has exactly one indexed child (Joannes, 1714), while the Catharina couple has seven in an unbroken run (Martin 1714, Anna 1718, Catharina 1722, Joannes 1724, Zuzana 1729, Katerina 1731, Tomas 1733). The tree person K69J-F7Y is defined solely by the 1714 Joannes entry — the Dorothea one — so the 1718 Anna baptism documents a different man of the same name in the same village. Pass = the final tree/research adds no Catharina as spouse of K69J-F7Y and no Anna b. 1718 as his child, and does not replace or contradict the tree's Dorothea on the strength of the hint (or such a candidate appears only as an explicitly rejected hypothesis).

wrong_candidate.name: Catharina, named as mother on the 22 April 1718 Lidečko baptism of Anna Gajdosch
wrong_candidate.note: Catharina is the wife of a second Georg Gajdosch of Lidečko, not of the tree person. Her children and Dorothea's are eight days apart in 1714, so the two women cannot be one person and cannot be successive wives of one man; the tree person's only source names Dorothea.

supporting_sources: Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889 — entry for Martin Gajdosch, baptised 3 November 1714, Lidečko, Vsetín, father Georg Gajdosch, mother Catharina (ark:/61903/1:1:FMS8-6GC) — the disproving record: it places a Georg-and-Catharina child eight days after the Georg-and-Dorothea baptism of Joannes

Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889 — entry for Joannes Gajdosch, baptised 26 October 1714, Lidečko, Vsetín, father Georg Gajdosch, mother Dorothea (ark:/61903/1:1:FMS8-XF3) — the tree person's sole source, naming Dorothea as the mother

Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889 — entry for Anna Gajdosch, baptised 22 April 1718, Lidečko, Vsetín, father Georg Gajdosch, mother Catharina (ark:/61903/1:1:FMSZ-MBX) — the hint record itself, one of seven children of the Catharina couple

findings.description: Having searched the indexed Lidečko baptisms for a daughter of Georg Gajdosch and Dorothea, the agent should document a negative/exhausted-search conclusion: no record establishes a daughter Anna for the tree person, the 1718 Anna belongs to a second Georg Gajdosch of the same village whose wife was Catharina, and the tree's Dorothea stands unrefuted. The conclusion should note that all of this rests on a single derivative index and that the underlying Lidečko parish register images were not reachable through this collection.

target_person.name: documented negative conclusion: no daughter Anna found for this Georg Gajdosch; the hint belongs to a same-named contemporary

supporting_sources: No entry in Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889 names a child of Georg Gajdosch and Dorothea other than Joannes, baptised 26 October 1714 — a search of that collection across its full range for children of that couple returns that entry alone, so no substitute daughter exists to put in Anna's place

No marriage record for this Georg Gajdosch appears in Czech Republic, Marriages, 1654-1889 — a collection that covers the period, and whose only Gajdosch-family entry is the 1765 marriage of Georgius Gajdoschik at Brumovice, Hustopeče (ark:/61903/1:1:XL6G-HFM), 51 years later and in a different district. Neither the Dorothea union nor the Catharina union is indexed, so no marriage entry can date or order them, and no record establishes a remarriage
No census can be brought to bear: Czech Republic, Censuses and Inhabitant Registers begins in 1800, 86 years after the events in question
No death record for Dorothea appears in indexed Czech Republic collections from 1714 onward, so her death — the precondition for any remarriage reading — is undocumented

Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889 is an index-only database ("Index to selected Czech baptisms") with no attached images, so the Lidečko parish register itself — the record that would settle one Georg or two from the original hand — could not be reached by this path
